newsitem.title: USA: NYC Water deal only gets $12 mln of retail orders.
newsitem.headline: NYC Water deal only gets $12 mln of retail orders.

text.p: The New York City Water Finance Authority on Monday said that retail investors had only ordered $12 million of bonds by the close of a two-day presale period, as demand was hurt by the market's recent big losses.
"It's a tough market," said a Water Finance official, who declined to be named.
The Authority early Monday sweetened the terms for retail investors, raising yields by 20 basis points, with a top yield of 5.40 percent in 2018.

When Treasuries on Friday tumbled just over two points because the latest economic data on payrolls and manufacturing showed surprising strength, reviving inflation fears, the Authority sold around $4 million of bonds to individual investors on the first day of the presale period.

Whether the size of the planned bond sale, which was pegged at $365 million, will be adjusted is a decision that will be made on Tuesday. Asked whether the offering's size would be cut, the official replied "I wouldn't draw any conclusions, probably lowered."
